_format: Map of preset name -> curated HTML snippet. Rendered inside <div class='preset-curated'> ABOVE the auto-generated voice table on the preset reference page. Keep prose tight: 1-3 sentences explaining (a) why this artist matters, (b) what technique the preset reproduces, (c) what to listen for. HTML allowed.
Oliveros — Deep A Resonance: Pauline Oliveros founded Deep Listening — the practice of letting a single sustained tone teach you to hear. This preset stacks four sine voices on a low A across two octaves and stages them in 60-second arrivals, mirroring her accordion drones that built incrementally over a session. Listen for the beat patterns between voices 1 and 2; that's where the meditation actually lives.
Riley — Rainbow Repetition: Terry Riley's In C (1964) introduced the cascade — same material entering at staggered times until the texture flowers. Four triangle voices in just-intonation C major enter at 0 / 15 / 45 / 90 s with ping-pong delay locked to eighth notes; the delay's 65% feedback turns each voice into a self-cascading echo within the larger cascade. Open the chord pill to swap to another root and the pattern still holds.
Radigue — Île Re-Sonante: Éliane Radigue spent decades coaxing music from a single ARP 2500 synthesiser, building works where the only events are infinitesimally slow timbral shifts. This preset uses two sine voices a perfect fifth apart with very slow amplitude LFOs (around 0.05 Hz, one full cycle ≈ 20 s) and long stereo reverb — the voices breathe past each other without ever quite landing in phase. Best with eyes closed at low volume.
Stars of the Lid — Orchestral Halo: Stars of the Lid (Adam Wiltzie + Brian McBride) built ambient music from sampled orchestral strings stretched into haloed pads. This preset uses sawtooth voices low-passed hard, with long reverb and a chord that blooms over 3 minutes via Replay × N timing — voice 1 at 0 s, voice 2 at 30 s, voice 3 at 90 s, voice 4 at 180 s. The result is the harmonic content slowly accumulating without you noticing when each new note arrived.
Sunn O))) — Onyx Tar: Sunn O))) (pronounced "sun") plays metal at one note per minute, with maximum amplifier saturation. This preset drops the chord into the sub-bass register, cranks drive on every voice, and stacks the same root across three octaves. Drop master volume first — the drive on this patch will absolutely melt your speakers at default level. The fourth voice is a high overtone meant to suggest the bowed-cymbal partials that ride above their riffs.
Basinski — Disintegration: William Basinski recorded a 1980s tape loop in 2001, only to watch its iron oxide flake off into his cassette deck across hours of playback. The recording of that decay became The Disintegration Loops. This preset uses pink-noise granular on voice 4 to mimic the tape-hiss layer, with the main melodic voices entering at 90 s — the long fade-in is the point. Pair with the WINDOW row's fade-in/out settings on a sample voice for the literal tape-decay effect.
Niblock — Tight Cluster: Phill Niblock sustained microtonal clusters at fortissimo for hours, recording dozens of takes of single notes by trombonists or cellists and layering them until beat frequencies thickened into a single inhuman timbre. This preset packs four sawtooths within a ~50-cent band so their fundamentals beat against each other; the resulting AM rhythm is what Niblock called "the unison." Use HEADPHONES — speakers can't reproduce the in-ear interference patterns.
Palestine — Strumming Overtones: Charlemagne Palestine sat at a Bösendorfer Imperial for hours hammering a single chord, letting the strings' upper partials emerge as audible melodies — what he called plus l'harmonie. This preset uses triangle voices with high reverb mix + long decay, and chorus on a slow rate to suggest the keyboard's micro-detuning. The chord template stays whatever you pick; the magic is in not changing it for a while.
Wada — Bagpipe Drone: Yoshi Wada built giant sirens and resurrected the Highland-pipe tradition with new technology, finding the sweet spot between folk and minimalism. This preset stacks a fifth + octave drone on sawtooth voices with stereo chorus and a touch of drive — the pipe character comes from the upper voice running a slow LFO on pitch that suggests reed instability. Set OSC 4's frequency by ear to a true just 7th over the root for the most authentic pipe colour.
Budd — Pearl Pad: Harold Budd played soft-pedalled Steinways through cascading reverb tanks; Brian Eno produced him. The preset uses sine voices with mild chorus and a very long reverb decay; the chord template defaults to a sus2 voicing because Budd's harmonic vocabulary was open and unresolved. Try it on top of a journey for an instant Eno-Budd The Plateaux of Mirror atmosphere.
Coltrane — Spiritual Organ: Alice Coltrane played Wurlitzer organ through a Leslie speaker into hours of devotional improvisation; her recordings under Swami Turiyasangitananda are the modal-jazz-ashram bridge. This preset uses sawtooth voices through chorus + delay to suggest the Leslie spread, with a Dorian-flavoured chord template. Open the Modal chord category and pick Dorian or Aeolian to lock it deeper into the spiritual-jazz idiom.
Earth — Tar Pit: Earth (Dylan Carlson) basically invented drone metal in 1990 with Earth 2 — slow downtuned riffs played at minimal tempo, no drums. This preset matches the doom register: square wave bass at a tritone interval with heavy drive and high-resonance low-pass — the resonant filter sweep is what Carlson got from his amp's tone stack. Bonus: open the DRIFT pill and pick Glacial Down to suggest detuning fatigue across a long session.
Nurse With Wound — Avant Tableau: Nurse With Wound (Steven Stapleton) defined unclassifiable European avant — collages, noise, dada, surreal sound art. This preset throws white noise + sample-and-hold LFO on filter cutoff to produce the bell-tone clatter that NWW used as connective tissue across albums. Combine with the granular waveform on voice 2 for the full Soliloquy for Lilith insectile rustle.
Haino — Spectral Shimmer: Keiji Haino plays guitar like he's exorcising it — feedback-driven, dynamics from silence to absolute saturation, sometimes with vocal screams folded in. The preset captures the high-end shimmer rather than the violence: bandpass filter at high Q sweeping slowly, high voices on sine + triangle. Pair with chorus on max width for the stereo phasing that Haino's amplifiers produce naturally.
